question: What is the primary purpose of a Quality Assurance Committee in a healthcare facility?

options.A: Procuring pharmaceutical drugs and medical equipment
options.B: Managing the hospital annual financial budget and payroll
options.C: Handling direct disciplinary actions for nursing staff
options.D: Systematically monitoring and improving patient care delivery

explanation: The core mandate of a Quality Assurance Committee is to evaluate and enhance the quality and safety of clinical services provided to patients. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h1)

question: How does the focus of a Quality Assurance Committee differ from routine ward management?

options.A: The committee operates independently of the hospital administration to provide legal counsel
options.B: Ward management focuses on macro-level policies while the committee handles daily bed allocation
options.C: Ward management deals exclusively with financial audits while the committee manages doctors
options.D: The committee takes a broad view of clinical processes and safety metrics rather than immediate daily shift logistics

explanation: While ward management tackles immediate operational needs like shift staffing, the QAC evaluates systemic clinical processes and institutional quality metrics. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why is a multidisciplinary structure essential for a Quality Assurance Committee?

options.A: Healthcare delivery involves diverse clinical and non-clinical inputs that require varied expertise
options.B: Government labor laws strictly mandate equal representation for all hospital departments
options.C: Medical doctors refuse to participate unless administrative staff are also present
options.D: It prevents any single nurse from being held responsible for clinical errors

explanation: Because patient care spans nursing, medicine, pharmacy, and administration, a diverse committee ensures comprehensive evaluation of clinical processes. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h2)

question: What specific expertise does the pharmacy representative bring to the quality assurance committee?

options.A: Approval of surgical rosters and theatre schedules
options.B: Expertise on medication safety and antimicrobial stewardship
options.C: Management of hospital facility maintenance and electrical supplies
options.D: Direct supervision of nursing medication administration charts

explanation: Pharmacists on the committee guide safe medication practices, review drug errors, and monitor rational drug use across the facility. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h2)

question: What is a primary activity of a clinical audit conducted by the quality assurance committee?

options.A: Checking patient case file compliance against established treatment protocols
options.B: Calculating the monthly salaries and allowances of clinical staff
options.C: Interviewing prospective nursing students for admission
options.D: Conducting physical maintenance checks on hospital generators

explanation: Clinical audits involve reviewing medical and nursing records to measure actual care delivery against established professional standards. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h3)

question: How do patient satisfaction surveys assist the Quality Assurance Committee?

options.A: By providing direct metrics to identify areas of poor service delivery and patient experience
options.B: By determining the exact financial profit generated by each hospital ward
options.C: By replacing the need for formal clinical audits and incident reporting
options.D: By serving as the primary legal defense during medical malpractice lawsuits

explanation: Analyzing patient feedback helps the committee pinpoint operational shortcomings and human relations gaps that affect overall hospital quality. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h3)

question: Which of the following is a key patient outcome indicator monitored by a quality assurance committee?

options.A: Daily cost of administrative printing paper
options.B: Frequency of cafeteria staff shift changes
options.D: Total number of hospital beds available

explanation: Tracking infection rates, mortality, and readmissions allows the committee to measure the safety and effectiveness of clinical care. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h4)

question: A hospital in a resource-limited setting notices an unexpected spike in surgical site infections. What is the most appropriate action for the Quality Assurance Committee to take?

options.A: Investigate both procedural compliance and environmental factors like water scarcity and sterilization protocols
options.B: Ignore the spike since infections are an inevitable consequence of surgery
options.C: Immediately terminate the employment of all surgical nurses on duty
options.D: Suspend all surgical operations permanently without further investigation

explanation: Effective QACs link adverse clinical outcomes to systemic factors, examining both human practice and environmental realities like water availability. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h4)

question: What is the main objective of integrating incident reporting into the quality assurance process?

options.A: Uncovering latent organizational flaws to prevent future recurrence
options.B: Justifying the reduction of nursing staff numbers on night shifts
options.C: Fulfilling legal requirements to increase health insurance payouts
options.D: Creating a permanent record for dismissing negligent staff members

explanation: Incident reporting is used by the committee to analyze system failures rather than to punish individuals, thereby improving patient safety. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h5)

question: Why is a blameless reporting culture crucial for effective incident management?

options.A: It ensures that patients never find out when a medical mistake occurs in the ward
options.B: It encourages healthcare workers to report errors and near-misses without fear of harsh punishment
options.C: It absolves the hospital management of all legal liability during malpractice claims
options.D: It eliminates the need for nurses to document interventions in the patient chart

explanation: When staff fear punishment, errors go unreported, hiding vital safety data that the committee needs to fix systemic issues. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h5)

question: What basis should guide the decisions and interventions of a Quality Assurance Committee?

options.A: Verbal complaints from patients received in the corridors
options.B: Empirical evidence and structured performance metrics
options.C: Intuition and guesswork from experienced nursing sisters
options.D: Personal opinions of senior hospital administrators

explanation: Quality assurance relies on objective data and measurable performance metrics rather than subjective impressions. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h6)

question: Why are tools like run charts or trend graphs useful in quality assurance data analysis?

options.A: They automatically calculate the monthly budget allocations for hospital wards
options.B: They help visualize performance data over time to identify specific patterns or improvements
options.C: They provide a legal contract between the patient and the attending physician
options.D: They replace the need for collecting patient mortality and morbidity statistics

explanation: Visual data tools allow the committee to track whether clinical indicators are improving, worsening, or remaining stable over time. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of a corrective action within a CAPA framework?

options.A: Drafting brand new hospital policies for future expansion
options.B: Reducing the overall operating budget of the clinical department
options.C: Eliminating the root cause of an existing error or non-conformity
options.D: Punishing the healthcare worker responsible for a clinical mistake

explanation: Corrective actions address problems that have already happened by fixing their underlying causes so they do not repeat. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h7)

question: How do preventive actions differ from corrective actions in healthcare quality management?

options.A: Preventive actions are handled exclusively by hospital accountants, while corrective actions are for nurses
options.B: Preventive actions apply only to equipment maintenance, while corrective actions apply to patient care
options.C: Preventive actions anticipate and block potential errors before they happen, whereas corrective actions fix existing ones
options.D: Preventive actions involve disciplining staff, whereas corrective actions involve giving financial rewards

explanation: Preventive actions are proactive measures designed to stop prospective failures before any patient harm occurs. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h7)

question: Which of the following is a common operational challenge faced by quality committees in resource-constrained settings?

options.A: An overwhelming surplus of digital computers and medical software
options.B: Excessive funding that causes confusion over budget allocation
options.C: Too many nurses available for every single shift in the wards
options.D: Staff shortages and heavy workloads leading to poor documentation habits

explanation: High patient-to-nurse ratios and heavy workloads frequently hinder consistent data collection and quality monitoring in busy wards. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h8)

question: What is a recommended best practice for sustaining committee effectiveness despite busy clinical environments?

options.A: Using simple audit tools and integrating feedback into existing ward handovers
options.B: Conducting mandatory eight-hour meetings for all staff every single week
options.C: Delegating all quality assurance responsibilities solely to student nurses
options.D: Eliminating all clinical audits until staffing levels return to normal

explanation: Streamlining processes and embedding quality discussions into routine routines like handovers prevents committee work from becoming an unmanageable burden. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h8)
